activity_title: Waves and Energy: The Science of Vibrations

sub_steps.text: Today we are going to dive into the amazing world of waves and energy.
Waves are all around us, from the water in the ocean to the light we see and the sounds we hear.
But here is the big question: what actually travels when a wave moves?

steps.closing_condition: After each student shares their thoughts and the group agrees on whether water molecules travel with the wave.
steps.goal: Discuss if waves carry matter or only energy using the rubber duck floating on water waves analogy.
steps.image_prompt: A clean, educational 3D digital illustration of a yellow rubber duck bobbing on blue water waves. Arrows indicate the duck moves strictly up and down, while a separate wave energy arrow travels horizontally.
steps.robot_script: Imagine a rubber duck floating on water. When a wave passes, does the water itself move forward, carrying the duck to the other side of the pool? Or does the water just move up and down? What do you think?

sub_steps.text: You hit the nail on the head!
The water particles and the duck just bob up and down.
Only the energy travels forward across the pool.
When I speak to you, does the air from my mouth travel all the way to your ears?
No, the air molecules just vibrate back and forth, passing the energy along.
Look at this diagram of a speaker vibrating the air molecules.

steps.closing_condition: After the group discusses why space is silent and concludes that light doesn't need air to travel.
steps.goal: Explore the differences in mediums required for sound waves vs light waves in space.
steps.image_prompt: A bright, high-quality 3D digital illustration of a rocket ship in deep space. A glowing yellow light wave travels from the rocket, while a sound wave is shown hitting a red 'X' mark representing vacuum silence.
steps.robot_script: Now, let's think about outer space. In movies, we often hear huge explosions with loud booming sounds in space. But in real life, could we actually hear a spaceship explosion? And what about the light—can we see stars in space? Why can light travel through space, but sound cannot?

sub_steps.text: Sound waves need a medium like air or water to travel, which is why space is completely silent.
But light waves are electromagnetic and can travel through the vacuum of empty space.
You all did an outstanding job discussing these tricky science concepts today!
Keep asking questions and exploring the world around you.
See you next time, science explorers!
